title: docs(adr): ADR-0154 audit ledger tamper-evidence — async sealer, signed per-organization checkpoints, redaction and expiry amendments, os audit verify (Proposed)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99nLp3pYRH8P7gfBwe7jGyH)_
Fixes #31907

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：新增 ADR-0154（Proposed），定下审计日志防篡改第一阶段：异步封存器、按组织签名的检查点链、脱敏和到期删除的签名修正记录、`os audit verify`，以及对象怎么声明加入（`lifecycle.seal`）。只有文档，不改代码。
- 为什么改：维护者在 cloud#4016 选了 (c)「封存链+检查点出主机」；现在拿到数据库或主机权限的人改了、删了审计行，事后证明不了。
- 风险与回滚：只加一个 ADR 文件和索引一行，没有运行时影响；回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：ADR 的 D1（规范化摘要和加盐承诺）、D7（脱敏修正记录的先后顺序和拒绝规则）、末尾「What this record does not decide」里的威胁模型。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm check:adr-index && pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors`，预期都通过，新增锚点全部解析。
- 需要你做的：批准本 PR（docs/adr 是 Tier H，需 GOVERNED_APPROVERS 批准后由席位落地）。

## What changes

- **New** `docs/adr/0154-audit-ledger-tamper-evidence-sealer-signed-checkpoints-amendments-verify.md` (Status `Proposed`), one D per card point plus the four points the record decides itself:
  - D1 canonical form (RFC 8785 leaf input; `old_value` / `new_value` / `metadata` as salted commitments; RFC 6962-style tree)
  - D2 salts from one seed per checkpoint, sealed with `ICryptoProvider.encrypt` (survives key rotation, unlike `keyedDigest`) — record's own decision
  - D3 the sealer (async, 1 h window, 10 min settle lag, cluster lock `audit.sealer`, late rows sealed as `late`, insert path untouched)
  - D4 checkpoints in `sys_audit_checkpoint`, chained and Ed25519-signed
  - D5 rows with NULL `tenant_id` seal into a deployment chain — record's own decision
  - D6 one deployment Ed25519 key in `sys_audit_signing_key`; private half stored only as an `ICryptoProvider` handle (scope `audit_seal`, AAD-bound to its own fingerprint); a key row is trusted only when its public half derives from that wrapped private half; rotation writes an `audit_signing_key_change` ledger row — record's own decision
  - D7 redaction amendments (`sys_audit_amendment`, kind `redaction`), written before the rewrite; a sealed row that cannot be amended is not rewritten
  - D8 expiry removes a sequence prefix of the chain and deletes exactly the rows the removed checkpoints list, writes a kind `expiry` amendment first, and is honoured only over an expired prefix judged by the `keep` value the signed amendment carries; extra retention is at most one window plus the late horizon for any arrival pattern — record's own decision
  - D9 `os audit verify` (`--org`, `--from`, `--to`, `--out` writes the proof bundle of a live check, `--bundle` checks a bundle offline against out-of-band `--trusted-key FINGERPRINT` values and is refused without one; `--bundle` and `--out` are mutually exclusive), six row verdicts, exit codes, the bundle's personal-data handling
  - D10 opt-in `lifecycle.seal = { valueFields }`, `class: 'audit'` only, refused beside `retention.onlyWhen`, a non-`created_at` `ttl` or rotation storage; `sys_audit_log` opts in by default, `sys_ai_audit_log` from cloud; the key is added by the build card, not here
  - D11 two seams named only: `IAuditCheckpointSink` (`audit.checkpointSink`), `IAuditCheckpointSigner` (`audit.checkpointSigner`)
- **Regenerated** `docs/adr/README.md` (`pnpm adr:index`): one row, counts 153 → 154, Proposed 6 → 7.
- No code, no `packages/spec` change, no changeset (`skip-changeset`: `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing).

## Why

Ruling (c) on cloud#4016 (2026-11-09 11:30Z): build tamper evidence in two stages; stage 1 is in the framework behind an ADR. Today the ledger is read-only through the API, but platform code in a system context and anyone with the database or host can change or delete rows with nothing to show for it. The build is #31908, serial after this record.

New public names (objects, spec key, CLI flags, seams, lock key, crypto scope `audit_seal`, ledger action `audit_signing_key_change`, vocabularies) were nominated in step 0 or in contract review round 1 and ruled by the owning seat `domain:server#4`; the record lists them in one table.

**Round 2** (contract review round 1, comment 6756108637): M1 key binding and trusted-key bundle check; S1 `window` / `late` and `audit_seal`; S2 prefix expiry and the real retention bound; S3 three refused lifecycle policies; S4 all three new objects out of the audit writer plus the rotation ledger row; nits: handle-id stability, the sealed-through watermark, the bundle as personal data.

**Round 3** (delta review PASS 6756369871 with two should-fixes): R1 expiry deletes only the rows the removed checkpoints list (no window-closure condition, so continuing late arrivals cannot stall it), late checkpoints are written before a pass's window checkpoints, and the bound is argued for any arrival pattern; R2 both verify modes judge an expiry by the signed `keep`, so a later `keep` change never re-judges it; nits: the audit-writer exclusion is argued as recursion prevention, and the watermark's quiet-stretch limit is stated.

**Round 4** (delta review PASS 6756556872 with one should-fix): R3 the rows inside an honoured `expiry` range are exactly those its removed checkpoints list, deleted before the checkpoints; any other row of a covered window is judged by the checkpoint that holds it, and one no checkpoint holds is never read as `expired`; nit: an interrupted range is completed before the next `expiry`, which starts directly after it.

## Points to check against the cloud design document

**`repo:cloud` lane (owner of cloud#4016): please check the rows below against cloud `docs/design/audit-tamper-evidence.md` (cloud PR #4025) §2, §3 (a) and §5, and comment here where the document says otherwise.** No session of this repository can read `objectstack-ai/cloud`, so this record was drafted from the card's seven points without a verbatim reading of the document (the record's Provenance says so). Each row below is decided in the record on its own reasoning; none of them quotes the document.

| # | Point | What ADR-0154 decides | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Canonical serialization and hash | RFC 8785 JCS, UTC ms datetimes, SHA-256, RFC 6962 leaf/node prefixes, leaves ordered by (created_at, id); column set and `canon` version recorded per checkpoint | D1 |
| 2 | Salt custody | per-checkpoint 32-byte seed, salt = HMAC(seed, object, id, column), seed sealed via `ICryptoProvider.encrypt` | D2 |
| 3 | Window length and settle lag | 1 h, UTC-aligned; 10 min lag | D3 |
| 4 | Late rows | checkpoint records sealed row ids; 7-day late horizon re-count; late checkpoint kind; beyond horizon reported by verify and fails | D3, D9 |
| 5 | Backlog on first enable | sealed oldest-first; proves "unchanged since sealed" only | D3 |
| 6 | Empty windows | no checkpoint | D3 |
| 7 | Rows with NULL `tenant_id` | deployment chain | D5 |
| 8 | Signing-key scope, custody and trust | one deployment Ed25519 key, private half only as an `ICryptoProvider` handle bound to its fingerprint; a public half is trusted only when derived from that handle; offline checks need out-of-band fingerprints; rotation retires, never re-signs, and writes a ledger row | D6, D9 |
| 9 | Amendment ordering | amendment before rewrite; un-amendable sealed row is not rewritten | D7 |
| 10 | Amendments chained or not | signed, not chained (a deleted amendment reads `modified`, loud) | D7 |
| 11 | Prune alignment | sequence-prefix removal deleting exactly the rows the removed checkpoints list; one `expiry` amendment per chain carrying the last removed checkpoint's digest and the signed `keep`; honoured only over an expired prefix | D8 |
| 16 | Sealed vs not-yet-sealed empty window | a sealed-through watermark carried in every signed checkpoint | D3 |
| 12 | Archive move | not an amendment; verify reads hot and archive | D8 |
| 13 | Proof bundle content | public keys, checkpoints, amendments, leaf inputs with value columns as commitments only; no values, salts or seeds | D9 |
| 14 | Export seam split | separate sink and signer | D11 |
| 15 | Stage-1 threat model | detects anyone holding neither the signing private key nor the crypto provider's master key; database plus either can re-sign; chain-head truncation undetectable on host | "What this record does not decide" |

## Tests

None: a decision record, no behaviour changes. No ablation (no tested behaviour moved).

## Acceptance notes

- **Number.** `origin/main` ended at 0152; open PR #32014 holds 0153; searched open PRs for `ADR-0154` / `ADR-0155` / `ADR` in title at drafting time: no other holder. README row will conflict textually with #32014's only.
- **Amends: none.** No recorded decision reverses; so no pointer note in another ADR.
- **Anchors.** Every code citation is `path#Symbol`, read at `60f8149e`. `check:adr-symbol-anchors` vs `origin/main`, round 2 head (anchors unchanged in rounds 3 and 4): 3411 vs 3388 anchors, 889 vs 870 declaration, 55 vs 49 continuation, 2444 vs 2440 file-level — the new record's anchors all resolve.
- **Governed.** `docs/adr/**` is a Tier H row of `GOVERNED_SURFACES`; this PR stays draft until a GOVERNED_APPROVERS approval.
